You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Do you mean any of the following: {'get_code_snippet(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZArchiveEntry.getCompressedSize())', 'get_code_snippet(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField.getCompressedSize())'}?"}

Diagnosis:
The failing test `testReadingOfFirstStoredEntry()` reads a ZIP entry from the archive `COMPRESS-264.zip` using `ZipArchiveInputStream` and expects the size of the first entry to be 5 and its contents to be exactly the byte array {'d', 'a', 't', 'a', '\n'}. According to the current bug report, this works fine with commons-compress 1.6 but yields NUL bytes or garbage data in commons-compress 1.7, indicating regression.

Looking at the code of `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()`, the method reads the local file header, decodes file name and extra fields, sets entry metadata, and opens streams based on compression. In this method, the entry size is read from the header if no data descriptor is present (`current.hasDataDescriptor`). This size is then returned by `ZipArchiveEntry.getSize()`, which simply returns the stored size field.

The test asserts the size of the entry by `getSize()`, which from the snippet is directly returning the internal size value set during header reading and extra processing (presumably in `processZip64Extra()`).

The actual reading of the entry data is done by reading from the stream (`IOUtils.toByteArray(in)`). The bug report suggests that in version 1.7, the data read is corrupted (NUL bytes instead of correct data).

In `closeEntry()`, the method ensures all entry bytes are read or skipped appropriately. The abnormal behavior could be caused if the entry stream setup in `getNextZipEntry()` is incomplete or incorrect, leading to reading garbage.

The core suspect is around reading or interpreting the ZIP local file header or handling the entry's data streams correctly.

Looking closely at `getNextZipEntry()`, after reading the local file header buffer, the code sets various fields such as platform, general purpose bit flag, method, time, CRC, compressed size, and uncompressed size. Notably, there is special treatment if the data descriptor flag is present.

The test zip file entry is stored (no compression), size 5 bytes. So the code path for `current.hasDataDescriptor == false` applies, where the sizes are set from the header.

The difference between versions 1.6 and 1.7 is probably in these header handling or the data stream setup (`current.in` field).

The issue likely is that in 1.7, the input stream for stored entries is not correctly set up or data length is misinterpreted, resulting in NUL bytes on reading, while in 1.6 the stream correctly returns the stored data.

Recent bug reports don't seem related to ZIP stream reading issues but to compression levels and 7z file compression, so they don't assist diagnosis here.

In summary, the root cause of the regression in 1.7 is probably from changes in `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()` that altered the setup or interpretation of entry data streams or size, resulting in wrong data read (NUL bytes) from stored entries, causing the test failure.

Potentially the method does not initialize `current.in` for stored (no compression) entries when the compressed size is present, or the data length is misread. Without `current.in` wrapping the underlying stream correctly, reading entry contents will yield incorrect bytes.

The fix probably needs to ensure that for stored entries (method == STORED) with compressed size known, `current.in` is set to read exactly that size from the underlying stream.

Suggested methods to investigate and fix:
- `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()`
- `ZipArchiveInputStream.closeEntry()` (to ensure entry data is read/skipped correctly)
- Possibly related helper methods handling stream setup for stored entries

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
